target_customer: Companies hiring remote contractors worldwide, and the freelancers they pay, mostly in Latin America and emerging markets
problem: Companies struggle to hire, contract and pay workers abroad, and workers face slow, expensive cross border payments and limited banking access.
business_model: SaaS fee per worker (priced at 29 USD per month per employee plus 1 percent of payment in Oct 2021, 49 USD per month contractor plan later) plus payment and wallet fees
product_category: global hiring, contractor payments and payroll fintech

founders.name: Santiago Aparicio
previous_startups: FitPal (LatAm gym aggregator, co-founded with Julian Torres)

founders.name: Julian Torres
previous_startups: Six startups founded in Colombia (per YC page)
founders.background_notes: YC page: bestselling author, Forbes contributor, entrepreneur in residence at InQlab.

founders.name: Jaime Abella
founders.background_notes: Named as CTO in Refresh Miami (spelled Abello in one place); the YC page does not list him.

competitors.name: Deel
competitors.what: Payroll and compliance platform to hire and pay contractors and employees globally
competitors.funding_then: 14M Series A (May 2020, Andreessen Horowitz) and 30M Series B (Sept 2020, Spark Capital), 48M total

technical_complexity.rationale: Payments across many countries, wallets and compliance workflows require licensed partners and integrations, but rest on existing rails rather than new technology.

defensibility.rationale: Many rivals with more capital offered similar contractor and EOR products. The two sided wallet gives some lock in once workers hold balances.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Deel raised 156M at 1.25B in April 2021 per TechCrunch, so a well funded rival was already building the wedge. Ontop still raised a 20M Series A in Oct 2021.

market_need_then: Remote work during the pandemic increased cross border hiring. Founders cited their own remote work experience as the idea source, and Refresh Miami reported 40 percent monthly growth and use in 67 countries by October 2021.

branding.domain_note: Uses getontop.com, a prefix domain rather than ontop.com.

identity.voice_and_tone: Confident, concise, benefit focused, for example 'Hire global contractors in minutes' (company site).

branding.community_and_virality: Named one of Forbes 30 Promising Startups in 2021 per a secondary profile; no merch or fan community found.

brand_strength.rationale: Generic English name with a get prefix domain and no brand specific press found.

outcome_analysis: Ontop joined YC in Winter 2021 as remote hiring boomed and raised a 20M Series A from Tiger Global and Point72 in October 2021, claiming 40 percent monthly growth and a team of about 200. The company is listed as active with 186 people. Well funded rivals such as Deel were ahead, so growth depended on a Latin America focus and the wallet product. Later rounds are unclear in sources.
notes: Series A confirmed by Refresh Miami (Oct 4, 2021) and Latamlist (Oct 6, 2021). Seed 4.5M led by Point72 comes from a Venture Capital Journal headline and Crunchbase snippet; its date was not found, so date is null. Aggregators conflict on totals (CB Insights 54.9M over 9 rounds including a 20M Series A-II dated Jan 2023, VCBacked 9M, FundedIQ 24.5M, Boring Business Nerd 35M) and are not recorded as rounds. Company says total 26M by Oct 2021. Education and prior employers other than FitPal not found. Deel funding date is from the 2020 TechCrunch and Business Wire items; Remote's 2021 round was not found. Outcome search found nothing about layoffs or acquisition.
